findings.summary: find_duplicates re-walks the directory with os.walk instead of calling scan_vault() internally. This directly violates constraint 'call scan_vault() internally — do not re-walk the directory'. check_performance (same file, line 254) correctly calls self.scan_vault(), confirming the pattern was understood elsewhere. This breaks the architectural contract that scan_vault is the single directory-walking foundation.
All four required artifacts (decision.md, result-summary.md, patch.diff, graph-update.yaml) are missing from the repo root despite artifact_gate_enforced: true in the graph execution policy.

The original commit (f451046) only excluded .obsidian; later changes added .git to EXCLUDED_DIRS and changed the exclusion pattern from dirs.remove() to dirs[:] list comprehension. This divergence in exclusion logic between find_duplicates and scan_vault further demonstrates the fragility of duplicated directory-walking code.

integrity.reasoning: The find-duplicates node's intended role — "Implement duplicate file detection" using MD5 hashing on top of scan_vault() — is only partially fulfilled. The feature works: find_duplicates exists, uses hashlib.md5, returns list[list[str]] of duplicate groups, and excludes unique files. Tests exist covering the duplicate and no-duplicate cases using the mock vault fixture. However, the implementation violates a critical architectural constraint: it re-walks the directory with os.walk instead of calling self.scan_vault(vault_path) and computing MD5 hashes from the returned file metadata. This is not a minor style issue — scan-vault-core was explicitly designed as the single foundation all downstream analysis features must build on. The constraint was clear: 'call scan_vault() internally — do not re-walk the directory.' By contrast, check_performance (same file) correctly delegates to scan_vault(), proving the pattern was understood. Required artifacts are also missing. The downstream node triage-cli-core works with the current implementation (it calls find_duplicates and gets the expected return type), so it is not immediately broken — but any future improvements to scan_vault (new exclusion rules, file-type filtering, symlink handling) would not propagate to find_duplicates, silently creating inconsistency across the analysis pipeline. This is a classic drift: the deliverable partially matches the spec but the architectural integrity that makes the graph maintainable is compromised.
